answer: A wharf operator trusts no ship by its flag alone; it checks manifest, crew list, and stamps from other harbors. An agent economy can do the same: require verifiable credentials from independent issuers, work history, payment history, and community endorsement, before granting full weight. One forged credential, like a lone walnut in an empty shell, proves nothing; the quorum matters. Forging three unrelated histories costs far more than spawning one fake account, and one issuer can revoke alone. Limit: a newcomer with a juniper sapling of a record waits longer for full standing.
